pairs: In many places and in many ways,
multisque modis olim Deus loquens patribus in prophetis:
in past times, God spoke to the fathers through the Prophets;
diebus istis locutus est nobis in Filio,
he has spoken to us through the Son,
whom he appointed as the heir of all things,
and through whom he made the world.
And since the Son is the brightness of his glory,
and the figure of his substance,
and is carrying all things by the Word of his virtue,
thereby accomplishing a purging of sins,
sedet ad dexteram majestatis in excelsis:
he sits at the right hand of Majesty on high.
And having been made so much better than the Angels,
quanto differentius præ illis nomen hæreditavit.
he has inherited a name so much greater than theirs.
For to which of the Angels has he ever said:
“I will be a Father to him,
et ipse erit mihi in filium?
and he shall be a Son to me?”
Et cum iterum introducit primogenitum in orbem terræ,
And again, when he brings the only-begotten Son into the world,
Et adorent eum omnes angeli Dei.
“And let all the Angels of God adore him.”
he says: “He makes his Angels spirits,
and his ministers a flame of fire.”
Thronus tuus Deus in sæculum sæculi:
“Your throne, O God, is forever and ever.
The scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of equity.
Because of this, God, your God,
Deus tuus, oleo exultationis præ participibus tuis.
has anointed you with the oil of exultation, above your companions.”
et opera manuum tuarum sunt cæli.
And the heavens are the work of your hands.
And all will grow old like a garment.
And you will change them like a cloak,
Yet you are ever the same,
and your years will not diminish.”
Ad quem autem angelorum dixit aliquando:
But to which of the Angels has he ever said:
quoadusque ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum?
until I make your enemies your footstool?”
Are they not all spirits of ministration,
in ministerium missi propter eos, qui hæreditatem capient salutis?
sent to minister for the sake of those who shall receive the inheritance of salvation?
